narrative.overview: ASoundJob's interface is a light mixing console: warm silver panels, recessed wells for inputs, raised caps for controls, and one fader-cap orange that lights up when something is live. The world is hardware-flat — bevels are single-pixel top highlights, never gradients or gloss. Every scannable number sets in a tabular monospace readout, the way meters and counters do on real gear.
keyCharacteristics: Light hardware world; dark only inside display windows
One interactive hue; state shown by illumination
Mono carries data, Archivo carries voice
Depth = affordance: wells sink, caps rise

rules.name: The One Fader Rule
rules.body: Orange marks interaction and nothing else; under 10% of any screen.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Any scanned number sets in Spline Sans Mono tabular figures; body prose never uses mono.

rules.name: The Spec Block Rule
rules.body: Job metadata renders as labeled mono pairs, never prose sentences.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: Things you type into sink; things you press rise.

dos: Do set every scannable number in Spline Sans Mono tabular figures.
Do express active state by filling the control orange, paired with aria-pressed or aria-current.
Do keep dark values inside display windows; pages stay light.
donts: Don't introduce a second interactive hue.
Don't use gradients, glass, or gloss.
Don't stack a legend label above a large display heading.
Don't render meter decoration without real data behind it.
